measures: LZc (LZ76 on spatially concatenated binarised Hilbert amplitude), ACE, SCE
reference: common average, then surface Laplacian (nearest neighbours)
data_per_condition_s: 2 min recorded per eyes condition -> 15 x 8 s epochs before rejection
epoch_selection: Artefactual channels removed/interpolated; epochs rejected by same criteria as TMS-EEG (visual); ICA removal of blink/eye-movement components; 9 of 62 channels analysed (F5,Fz,F6,C6,Cz,C6,P5,Pz,P6)

measures: PCI (LZ76 on binarised significant-source matrix)

quote: using a 1 Hz high pass filter and 45 Hz low pass filter (Hamming window sinc FIR filter) ... Data in the interval 8-300 ms after the pulse ... used to derive the PCI
notes: Follows PCI developers' pipeline (Casali 2013 et al.). MNI template head model.

measures: graph theory on Fourier cross-spectral matrices (strength, clustering, local efficiency, path length); 1/f slope (alpha)

notes: Reanalysis of Oxford 'bench' dataset (Ni Mhuircheartaigh 2013; Zenodo 1168447). Not a complexity paper. Baseline = start of propofol infusion, not eyes-closed rest. Robustness check at 62.5 Hz.

measures: LZc, LZs, LZcN, LZsN (phase-randomised normalised), ACE, ACEN, SCE, SCEN

quote: All MEG recordings were band-pass filtered (1–150 Hz), downsampled to 600 Hz and segmented into epochs of 2 sec length.
notes: LZ78 dictionary encoding. Binarisation: Hilbert instantaneous amplitude thresholded at its mean per channel per 2 s segment (1200 samples). LZc = channels concatenated observation-by-observation (spatiotemporal); LZs = single channel. Normalised by value for randomly shuffled sequence; _N variants divided by mean of phase-randomised surrogates (per channel per segment). SCE uses phase difference <0.8 rad (mod 2pi) synchrony binarisation. 30 Hz LPF applied to all datasets because of residual muscle artefact in LSD data. Spectral power computed WITHOUT the 30 Hz LPF. Values per segment then averaged across segments per subject. Dataset via Carhart-Harris 2016 PNAS, which reports two resting MEG scans totalling 14 min and states power results for eyes-closed rest; Schartner states open eyes - unresolved discrepancy. Subjects supine.

study: Toker 2022 PNAS [LSD MEG, modified 0-1 chaos test]
measures: modified 0-1 chaos test K (chaoticity); edge-of-chaos criticality c (alpha=0.85 for main)

lpf_hz: channel- and trial-specific, FOOOF-selected in 1-6 Hz (upper edge of slowest oscillation peak); mean 3.27 Hz, SD 0.48 across all datasets

data_per_condition_s: NR (channel x trial counts in SI Table S5)

quote: MEG data were split into 10-second trials, demeaned, detrended, and bandstop filtered at 50 Hz and harmonics
notes: Data via Carhart-Harris 2016 (19 recorded, 3 excluded). Chaos: FOOOF on 1-6 Hz per channel x trial; channel-trials with no peak in 1-6 Hz excluded (LSD 7-32% excluded, SI Table S1). Discretisation by taking local minima/maxima; signals normalised to SD 0.5, noise sigma=0.5; K median over 100 random c in (0,2pi); trial K = median across channels; subject = median over trials. LPF frequency used as covariate. Fixed-cutoff LPF gave similar but less consistent results (SI Fig S7). Main text cites ref 100 (Muthukumaraswamy 2013 psilocybin) as psychedelic data source, but SI describes LSD data citing Carhart-Harris 2016 - citation inconsistency. Model/data matched to 10 s at 500 Hz (5000 samples). | access detail: full_text (main + SI)

measures: LZ (broadband Lempel-Ziv of median-split z-scored Hilbert instantaneous amplitude)

epoch_selection: EEGLAB automatic bad-channel detection (kurtosis/probability threshold 5; mean 30% channels rejected, max 8); 21.3 +/- 13.7 epochs rejected per subject; Infomax ICA (2.7 +/- 1.1 components removed)
eyes: baseline EC and EO (5 min each); DMT condition NR
quote: Data was divided into 2 s. epochs and the first 5 epochs were removed for all subjects and conditions. Data was bandpass-filtered (1 – 90 Hz) and notch-filtered (47.5 – 52.5 Hz).
notes: Journal verified: J Psychopharmacol 2021;35(4):406-420 (not NeuroImage). The user's 'NeuroImage' is probably Pallavicini 2019 NeuroImage (MEG spectral signatures of LSD/psilocybin/ketamine, which has no complexity measure). Values taken from the preprint. The preprint abstract reports 'widespread increases in signal complexity', but the published abstract does not mention complexity (the published keywords still list 'complexity'); whether LZ was kept in the published version could not be checked. Binarisation is a median split after z-scoring (equal 0/1 proportion in all channels). Shuffle normalisation NR; whether LZ was per channel or on concatenated data is NR (per-channel t-maps suggest per channel). Result: LZ increased at all channels for DMT vs EC, similar in size to EO vs EC, so the eyes-open confound is unresolved. Also reports metastability/synchrony (Kuramoto), which are not complexity measures. Companion Tagliazucchi 2021 Front Psychiatry (same dataset) has no complexity measure. | access detail: full_text (bioRxiv preprint 10.1101/2020.08.19.258145); published J Psychopharmacol version paywalled

agent: 5-MeO-DMT 12 mg synthetic, inhaled (vaporised, single breath) in retreat setting; uncontrolled (pre-dose resting baseline as comparator)
n_subjects: 19 analysed (29 tested; 10 excluded for >50% artefact in first 10 min, 1 for bridging); 13 with artefact-free peak window
measures: maximal Lyapunov exponent (Rosenstein algorithm on broadband Hilbert amplitude envelope, Takens embedding); automutual-information (AMI) decay time/intrinsic timescale on broadband signal. No LZ or entropy-rate measure
data_per_condition_s: baseline 420 (140 x 3 s epochs, before rejection); drug 1200 (400 x 3 s epochs, before rejection); peak window 1.5-2.5 min post-inhalation (n=13) used for flow analyses
epoch_selection: bad channels interpolated; extended Infomax ICA (40 components); manual epoch rejection; subjects excluded if >50% of first 10 min needed removal
quote: Data was filtered using a finite impulse response (FIR) one-pass, zero-phase, non-causal bandpass filter at 0.1-50 Hz. ... segmented into non-overlapping 3s epochs
notes: Values from the preprint, whose title differs ('Complex slow waves radically reorganise human brain dynamics under 5-MeO-DMT'); the Cell Rep version could not be checked. The preprint gives no embedding dimension, delay or window length for the Lyapunov exponent, no window length for AMI, and does not say which data segment either was computed on. Results: lambda_max fell slightly (p_FDR=0.046); AMI decay time roughly doubled (221.9 to 495.3 ms, p_FDR=0.018). Shannon entropy appears only inside a mutual-information recurrence analysis of velocity fields. ANT Neuro Waveguard 64-ch saline net, NA-261 amplifier. | access detail: full_text (bioRxiv preprint 10.1101/2024.10.04.616717); Cell Reports version is OA but returned 403

agent: inhaled freebase DMT 20 mg and 40 mg (single long inhalation), naturalistic setting, blinded counterbalanced; drug-free resting-state comparison
n_subjects: 19 (2 DMT sessions and 1 RS session excluded after preprocessing)
measures: LZc (channels in a region concatenated, median-binarised raw signal, shuffle-normalised); LZsum (per-channel LZ averaged); permutation entropy (k=3, tau=1,2,4,8); also wSMI/wPLI connectivity, specparam spectral/aperiodic features
data_per_condition_s: RS 600 (10 min, first 5 s removed); DMT 1200 (20 min from exhalation); minus rejected epochs (RS 7.9 +/- 4.1, DMT 24.3 +/- 15.2)
epoch_selection: automatic rejection of epochs exceeding +/-500 uV, +/-2 SD single-channel amplitude or +/-6 SD all channels, plus manual scan; kurtosis-based channel rejection (threshold 5); ICA per condition/session; sessions with >50% epochs removed excluded
n_channels: 32 (BrainProducts BrainAmp); summarised by region medians (frontal, central, parietal, occipital, temporal, global)
quote: The EEG data was filtered between 0.5 and 45Hz. ... EEG data was re-referenced to the average signal, and split into five second epochs (1,250 samples).
notes: LZ binarises the raw EEG around its median (no Hilbert envelope). LZc is normalised by a shuffled copy (Schartner 2015); the text does not say whether LZsum is normalised. PE tau values map to roughly 30-45 Hz (tau=1), 15-29 (2), 8-14 (4) and 4-7 Hz (8) at 250 Hz. Features are medians over the electrodes in each region. Alpha power and PE tracked the TET experience dimensions most strongly, and LZ most weakly. Same Buenos Aires group as Pallavicini 2021. | access detail: full_text (author accepted manuscript, Cambridge repository; bioRxiv 10.1101/2024.12.19.629418)

measures: Lempel-Ziv-Welch (LZW) complexity, Higuchi fractal dimension (HFD), permutation entropy (PE), waveform complexity (WC); also wSMI connectivity, BAR, FAA
epoch_selection: NR
quote: NR (abstract only): "Four complexity measures were evaluated: Lempel-Ziv-Welch (LZW) complexity, Higuchi fractal dimension (HFD), permutation entropy (PE), and waveform complexity (WC)."
notes: Abstract says complexity was computed per frequency band: under DMT, HFD and PE increased in beta/gamma and decreased in delta/theta/alpha, and complexity correlated with intensity ratings. Coauthors include Timmermann and Carhart-Harris, and n=13 IV DMT vs placebo matches the Timmermann 2019 cohort, but the abstract does not confirm the dataset is the same. Band edges, filters and epochs would need the full text. Starlab/Neuroelectrics group (Ruffini). | access detail: abstract_only (paywalled; ScienceDirect 403)

agent: 5-MeO-DMT benzoate (BPL-003) intranasal 5 mg and 12 mg vs saline nasal-spray placebo; one expert meditator
measures: entropy rate = normalised LZ76 complexity (mean-binarised per 3-s epoch); per channel and channel-average
reference: Cz online; re-referenced to average after interpolation
epoch_overlap: NR for LZ (spectral analysis used 50% overlap)
data_per_condition_s: drug/placebo: window 4.7-6.9 min post-administration (~132 s); compared with preceding 8-min eyes-open baseline (mind-wandering part); meditation: 17 x 10-s segments
epoch_selection: visual removal of noisy channels and segments with gross/muscle artefacts; ICA (cardiac, eye, line noise); window chosen by participant-indicated most immersive moment in 12 mg session (video review)
eyes: EO (instructed eyes open; window chosen before participant closed eyes in 12 mg session)
n_channels: 256-channel EGI HydroCel net minus neck/face channels (number analysed NR)
quote: Data was downsampled to 250Hz, demeaned, and then band-passed filtered at 0.5-45Hz. ... The signal was binarized by employing the mean of each 3-second epoch.
notes: Case report (n=1), not peer reviewed. High-dose 12 mg increased average entropy rate vs its baseline; 5 mg and meditation decreased it. The normalisation method behind 'entropy rate' is not specified. Statistics: cluster permutation over channels (7000 perms) on epochs as trials; channel-average permutation test (10,000 perms), FDR-corrected. | access detail: full_text (PsyArXiv preprint v2)

study: Blackburne 2026 bioRxiv [DMT and 5-MeO-DMT EEG subsets of 5-drug info-decomposition]
agent: DMT (dataset ref. 27 of the paper, not identified in accessible text) and 5-MeO-DMT (Blackburne 2025 Cell Rep dataset); also LSD, psilocybin, ketamine MEG (other batches)
modality: EEG source-localised (DMT, 5-MeO-DMT); MEG for other compounds
n_subjects: N=80 across all five compounds; per-dataset n NR in accessible text
measures: state-space entropy rate (complexity; Mediano CSER-type estimator, ref. 31) per AAL-90 region; also AIS, TDMI, transfer entropy (Gaussian VAR), PhiID atoms
reference: NR (source-localised to AAL-90; localisation method NR in main text)
epoch_s: >=2 (epochs truncated to a minimum length of 2 s)
epoch_selection: NR in main text (acquisition details in Supplementary S1, not accessed)
quote: bandpass filtering to 1–50 Hz with a zero-phase 2nd-order elliptic filter, downsampling to 100 Hz with integer decimation
notes: All five datasets were re-preprocessed in one common pipeline, so the filter/epoch settings here replace those of the original papers. Epochs are treated as stationary realisations, and the entropy-rate estimator's parameters are not stated in the main text. Across all five drugs, the change in entropy rate is strongly anti-correlated with the change in AIS. Per-drug entropy-rate values for DMT are not in the main text. Not peer reviewed. Overlaps with the 5-MeO-DMT row (Blackburne 2025) and probably a Timmermann DMT dataset, so do not double count. | access detail: full_text (bioRxiv preprint main text; Supplementary S1 with dataset details not accessed)

agent: psilocybin (Psilocybe cubensis 0.5 g dried mushroom, microdose)
n_subjects: 34 recruited (EEG n analysed NR in text)
measures: LZ (broadband)
epoch_s: 2 (preprocessing epochs; LZ window not explicitly stated)
data_per_condition_s: 300 recorded per eyes condition (post-rejection amount NR)
epoch_selection: EEGLAB automatic flagging + visual inspection before rejection; Infomax ICA artifact removal; bad channels (kurtosis/probability) interpolated
time_since_dose: NR in text (dosing-day timeline in Fig. 1c)
quote: First, time series were bandpass-filtered (1–90 Hz) and notch-filtered (47.5–52.5 Hz)... Next, time series were divided into 2 s epochs.
notes: Microdose study (sub-perceptual, double-blind within-subject). LZ on binary series from median split of Hilbert envelope after z-scoring (Schartner-style). 'Global' LZ reported plus topography -> computed per channel. No LZ difference vs placebo; theta power decreased (EC). mBrainTrain mobile 24-ch amp, 0-250 Hz hardware passband.

agent: LSD 13 and 26 ug sublingual (low dose); also THC and methamphetamine comparison studies
measures: LZ76 (single-channel, normalized)
filter_type: acquisition filters: HP 1 Hz, LP 60 Hz (-12 dB/octave)
epoch_selection: manual removal of artifactual channels and continuous-data periods; ICA removal of eye/heart/muscle
quote: EEG recordings were high pass filtered (1 Hz), and low pass filtered (60 Hz, -12 dB/octave)... digitized (16 bit/ 500 Hz sampling rate)
notes: Filter/fs details from Supplemental Methods (Springer ESM). Binarized at signal mean; normalized C*log2(n)/n; computed per channel and averaged across 10-20 electrodes. Epoch/segment length for LZ not reported (possibly whole 5-min record; not stated). LSD dose-dependently increased LZ; THC and MA did not. Within-subject placebo, 3 sessions.

n_subjects: 22 analysed (25 recruited; 3 excluded for TMS-EEG response criterion)
measures: LZc (multichannel concatenated), LZs (single channel), phase-shuffle-normalized LZsN/LZcN
filter_type: detrend + 1st-order HP 0.01 Hz, then Butterworth 0.5/40 Hz, notch 50 Hz
epoch_selection: 2-s segmentation for bad-channel and bad-epoch rejection before ICA; only contiguous clean 2-s runs concatenated to 10-s; LZc averaged using only values between 25th-75th percentile
eyes: both (5 min EO then 5 min EC; analysed separately)
quote: Recordings were segmented into 10-s epochs and the LZc of each epoch was calculated. LZc has been demonstrated to be sensitive to decreasing epoch lengths
notes: Paper literally says 'low- and high-pass Butterworth filtering of 0.5 and 40 Hz, respectively' (wording swapped; interpreted as 0.5-40 band). Binarization: thresholding of analytic signal (threshold stat not specified; 'relative to a statistically defined threshold'). LZc increased under psilocybin EC (p<1e-3) not EO. Phase-shuffle normalization reduced effects. Authors explicitly chose 10-s epochs because of epoch-length sensitivity.

measures: PCI (source LZ, Casali 2013), PCI-ST (sensor)
filter_type: pulse artifact mirroring (-2 to +5 ms), moving average, polynomial detrend, 1-45 Hz filter (design NR), 50 Hz line-noise filter
epoch_s: evoked: PCI over 8-300 ms post-TMS (trial-averaged); trials 2000-2500 ms ISI
data_per_condition_s: 200 TMS pulses per site (~7 min) x 3 sites
epoch_selection: bad channel and trial rejection; ICA for ocular/cardiac/muscle/TMS artifacts
time_since_dose: after resting EEG at 60 min (~60-120 min)
quote: 1–45 Hz filtering was used with a 50 Hz line noise filter... The data was downsampled from 5000 Hz to 1000 Hz
notes: Evoked complexity, not spontaneous. PCI: wMNE source modelling, nonparametric bootstrap (alpha=0.01) binarization vs pre-TMS baseline, LZ normalized by source entropy. PCI-ST: PCA (99% variance) + recurrence quantification at sensor level. PCI unchanged by psilocybin. 8-300 ms window from Fig. 2C legend (time-resolved PCI).

measures: LZC (broadband 1-120 Hz main; band-limited in Fig. S5)
filter_type: MNE v1.8 Raw.filter band-pass (design NR); notch 50 and 100 Hz
reference: source: dSPM (identity noise cov, loose=0.2) on ico5, HCP-MMP 360 parcels
epoch_selection: visual inspection; Autoreject (mask) -> Picard ICA -> 2nd Autoreject pass; ~200 epochs/run retained
quote: LZC was computed by concatenating all artifact-free epochs. The binarization threshold was set to the average of the signal.
notes: Reanalysis of Carhart-Harris 2016 PNAS dataset. Raw signal (not Hilbert envelope) mean-binarized; normalized LZC = log(n)/n * LZC_raw. Per parcel. Band-limited LZC also reported (alpha to high-gamma).

measures: Higuchi fractal dimension (kmax=18)
filter_type: MNE v1.8 Raw.filter band-pass (design NR); notch 50 and 100 Hz
epoch_selection: as LZC row (Autoreject/ICA/Autoreject)
quote: We computed the HFDs for each epoch, and subsequently averaged over epochs within each recording.
notes: antropy higuchi_fd; kmax chosen by knee detection on HFD-vs-kmax curve over [2,50] -> 18. LSD increased HFD. 2-s epochs following Carhart-Harris 2016.

agent: psilocybin 25 mg oral + IV midazolam (open label)
measures: LZCn (LZ76, phase-shuffle normalized); spectral exponent
filter_type: 1st-order IIR HP 0.1 Hz + 2-way least-squares FIR band-pass 1-50 Hz
data_per_condition_s: per time point 7-535 s (mean 242 s, 0.11-8.92 min)
epoch_selection: visual rejection of artifactual segments; AMICA x2; ICLabel-type removal (<85% neural confidence)
quote: For each channel, the EEG data were first split up into 4 s nonoverlapping segments (2000 samples each).
notes: Binarized by median of Hilbert amplitude; normalized by N/log2(N), then by mean of 100 phase-shuffled surrogates. No placebo; within-session baseline. Music on except 30 and 120 min. Midazolam confound.

agent: psilocybin 25 mg vs 1 mg oral (fixed order)
n_subjects: 28 enrolled (EEG-usable n NR in main text; 18 in Godfrey 2025 same cohort)
measures: LZc ('brain entropy'); spectral power
reference: average (online Pz; A1/A2 earlobe noise subtraction)
epoch_selection: visual inspection, noisy segments removed, channels interpolated; ICA blink removal
quote: rsEEG data were band-passed filtered at 1-45 Hz... Next, data was re-referenced to the average and segmented in 2 s-epochs.
notes: LZc computation details not in main text; same cohort/pipeline as Godfrey 2025 (mean-binarized LZ76, 2-s epochs averaged over epochs and channels). LZc at 1-2 h predicted next-day insight and 1-month well-being. Dry electrodes.

measures: LZc (LZ76)
epoch_selection: removal of artifacts/noisy channels with interpolation; ICA blink removal
quote: The pre-processed, broadband (1–45 Hz) data was segmented into 2 s, non-overlapping epochs and absolute LZc was calculated as the average over all epochs and all channels
notes: Binarized by comparing signal to its mean (raw signal, not envelope). Same Imperial psilocybin-naive cohort as Lyons 2026 (Lyons states 4-min recordings; Godfrey states 5 min).

agent: psilocybin mushrooms 3 g vs 0.5 g dried (self-blinded naturalistic)
measures: LZc (broadband)
filter_type: band-pass (MNE; design NR) + notch 50 Hz and harmonics
epoch_selection: autoreject + manual inspection; ICA; subjects with <50 valid epochs excluded
quote: A band-pass filter with a frequency range of 0.5–90 Hz was applied... The filtered data were then segmented into fixed-length epochs of 2 s
notes: Hilbert envelope, z-scored, median-split binarization; LZc per epoch and channel, averaged over epochs (per-channel). Comparison is high vs low dose (no inactive placebo). Same Buenos Aires mBrainTrain setup as Cavanna 2022.

measures: LZ76 (entropy-rate normalized); CSER (state-space entropy rate, band-integrated)
data_per_condition_s: 300 recorded per time point (recordings dropped if >60% removed)
epoch_selection: expert visual marking of artifacts; ICA eye/ECG; sleep/drowsiness epochs marked and removed by sleep specialist
quote: Data was parceled into 4 second epochs with 1 second overlap... applied to 4-seconds segments Z-scored EEG downsampled to 250Hz data
notes: Extracted from medRxiv v1 JATS XML; published J Psychopharmacol 2026 (doi 10.1177/02698811261473445, paywalled) reports gamma-band signal diversity increase 1-3 h (CSER band decomposition). LZ averaged over channels and epochs (no concatenation); binarization threshold NR. CSER computed broadband then decomposed into bands (no pre-filtering). Placebo crossover. | access detail: full_text (preprint); published version paywalled

agent: ketamine (racemic, IV, subanaesthetic; stepwise 0.1-1.0 mg/kg/h, median maintained 0.7 mg/kg/h)
measures: LZc (spatiotemporal, concatenated channels), ACE, SCE
data_per_condition_s: ~120 (15 x 8 s epochs per condition, before rejection; 2-min recordings)
epoch_selection: 2-min recording split into 8 s non-overlapping segments; artefactual epochs rejected (same criteria as TMS-EEG: visual); ICA for blinks/eye movements
n_channels: 9 (of 62; chosen to limit state space for entropy estimates)
time_since_dose: during maintained infusion once subject and anaesthesiologist certain of drug effect (median infusion time 43.5 min total)
quote: the data were split into 8-second non-overlapping segments, resulting in 15 epochs per condition ... filtered with a 0.5 Hz high pass and 45 Hz low pass filter (Hamming window sinc FIR filter
notes: Methods as in Schartner 2015 (ref 10). Hilbert transform then binarised at mean absolute amplitude (ACE, LZc); SCE uses phase-synchrony threshold 0.8 rad. LZc = LZ76 on spatially concatenated binarised matrix, normalised by LZc of time-shuffled data. Baseline correction = epoch mean. Open-label, no placebo; baseline same day before infusion. Also 1000 Hz hardware LPF at acquisition.

measures: PCI (LZ76 on binarised source-space significance matrix)
epoch_s: 0.292 (8-300 ms post-pulse window of trial-averaged response); baseline -500 to -5 ms
epoch_selection: visual rejection of artefactual trials/channels; -2 to 5 ms around pulse removed; ICA for residual artefacts

time_since_dose: during maintained infusion after noticeable drug effect reported
quote: signals were referenced to the common average reference, using a 1 Hz high pass filter and 45 Hz low pass filter (Hamming window sinc FIR filter) ... downsampled to 312.5 Hz
notes: PCI per Casali 2013: sources binarised by bootstrap baseline threshold (99th percentile), LZc normalised by asymptotic maximum given proportion of 1s; source entropy threshold 0.08. No significant change in PCI under ketamine.

agent: ketamine (racemic, IV): subanaesthetic 0.5 mg/kg over 40 min infusion; also anaesthetic 1.5 mg/kg bolus
measures: spatiotemporal LZC (Casali-style), normalised by spatial shuffle and by phase-randomised surrogates (LZC_N); temporospatial LZC supplementary
fs_hz: 250 (recorded 500, downsampled); HMM run at 125 Hz on 2 virtual channels
hpf_hz: NR (no explicit high-pass; local linear detrending, 2 s window, 1 s step, Chronux)
epoch_overlap: NR (1-s epochs extracted from HMM-state-smoothed time series)
data_per_condition_s: <=30 (random subset of at most 30 x 1-s epochs per HMM state per participant), drawn from last 5 min of subanaesthetic infusion (baseline/recovery: first 2 min)
epoch_selection: visual rejection of noisy segments; HMM-MAR (K=5) on frontal/posterior averages; HMM state time course smoothed with 1-s moving average; 1-s epochs assigned to states; random <=30 per state
time_since_dose: last 5 min of the 40-min subanaesthetic infusion (assumed steady state)
quote: the EEG signal was detrended using a local linear regression method with a 2-s window at a 1-s step size ... lowpass filtered at 50 Hz via butterworth filter of order 5
notes: Anaesthetic condition (LOC to ROC, ~10 min) analysed with same pipeline (state-specific; anaesthetic part out of scope). Hilbert amplitude binarised at per-channel mean. Supplementary checks with 0.5-s (max 60) and 2-s (max 12) epochs. Complexity is per HMM state, not per behavioural condition; subanaesthetic dominated by one HMM state. Overlaps Vlisides 2017/2018 cohort.

agent: ketamine (racemic, IV TCI, Domino model): 0.2 and 0.4 ug/ml subanaesthetic; 1.0 ug/ml anaesthetic
measures: dynamical criticality / stability: moduli of eigenvalues (criticality index) of first-order multivariate AR model
filter_type: Butterworth 4th order bandpass, zero-phase (filtfilt); CleanLine 60 Hz + harmonics
epoch_selection: 1 continuous artifact-free minute per dose chosen by visual inspection within period of stable predicted plasma concentration; ICA/ICLabel; bad channels interpolated
time_since_dose: during steady predicted plasma concentration at each TCI step (escalating within one session)
quote: A bandpass fourth-order Butterworth filter with cutoff frequencies at 0.5 and 200 Hz was applied ... In this case we used time windows of length 0.5 s.
notes: AR order 1 fitted with arfit per 0.5-s window across all 82 channels; preliminary tests of order 1-4 and windows 0.25-2 s reportedly did not change fit. Surrogate: random time-shift per channel. Includes anaesthetic dose 1.0 ug/ml (out of scope) in same pipeline. 2-min EC rest recordings.

agent: ketamine (racemic, IV 0.54 mg/kg over 30 min: 0.27 mg/kg load + 0.27 mg/kg over 20 min); saline placebo session 7 days earlier
measures: temporospatial LZC (LZC_T) and spatiotemporal LZC (LZC_S)
epoch_s: NR for LZC_T (computed on first 10 min of recording); LZC_S in 60 s blocks and over whole 10 min
epoch_selection: manual artefact removal (DeepPsy software), ICA for eye/cardioballistic/technical artefacts; details via Ip 2024

time_since_dose: start-infusion: 10 min after first (loading) infusion; end-infusion: 20 min after second infusion; also pre and 24 h

notes: Hilbert instantaneous amplitude binarised at MEDIAN; LZC_T normalised vs randomly shuffled sequence; computation per Aamodt 2023; LZC_T/LZC_S definitions via Li & Mashour 2019/Casali 2013. Single-blind fixed sequence (placebo first). Preprocessing details via Ip et al. 2024. | access detail: full_text (author manuscript on Zenodo 15517660; journal version paywalled)

agent: ketamine (racemic, IV, 40-min infusion; 0.1/0.25/0.5 mg/kg) vs midazolam 0.03 mg/kg
n_subjects: 33 randomised late-life TRD veterans (18 ketamine analysed incl. dose groups; 29 total analysed)
measures: LZC (single-channel, mean across channels)
filter_type: independent high-pass and low-pass filters (type NR); CleanLine 60 Hz + harmonics
data_per_condition_s: 100 (first 110 s of EC rest, first 10 s discarded)
epoch_selection: first 110 s of EC recording, first 10 s excluded; ASR for bad channels/bursts; ICA (FastICA, MARA/TESA)

time_since_dose: 30 min after infusion start (during 40-min infusion), 60, 120, 240 min, 24 h, 7 d
quote: Resting state signals were filtered using independent high-pass (1 Hz) and low-pass (50 Hz) filters and resampled to 250 Hz ... providing an analysis window of 100 s (25,000 samples)
notes: Hilbert transform then binarised at mean of rectified signal (per Schartner 2015); normalised by shuffled surrogate. Abstract says LZC/MSE increased '30 min post-infusion' but Methods say EEG at '30 min post-start of infusion' (during infusion). Days-later (24 h, 7 d) also measured. Doses pooled across ketamine groups.

agent: ketamine (racemic, IV, 40-min infusion; 0.1/0.25/0.5 mg/kg) vs midazolam 0.03 mg/kg
measures: multiscale entropy (sample entropy, 20 scales, m=2, r=0.5; binned 1-5, 6-10, 11-15, 16-20)
filter_type: independent high-pass and low-pass filters (type NR); CleanLine 60 Hz
data_per_condition_s: 100 (same 100-s segment as LZC, 25 x 4 s epochs)
epoch_selection: same segment as LZC (first 110 s minus first 10 s); ASR + ICA
time_since_dose: 30 min after infusion start (during infusion), 60, 120, 240 min, 24 h, 7 d
quote: we computed MSE on non-overlapping 4 s epochs and averaged across the epochs to achieve the final MSE estimate
notes: r=0.5 (x SD presumably; stated only 'r of 0.5'). Per-channel then averaged.

agent: ketamine (racemic, IV, 40-min infusion; 0.1/0.25/0.5 mg/kg) vs midazolam (same trial as Murphy 2023, NCT02556606)
measures: high-order interactions: TC, DTC, O-information, S-information (Gaussian-copula entropy; THOI package)
filter_type: FIR bandpass; CleanLine 59-61 Hz; then band-specific bandpass theta 4-7, alpha 8-12, beta 12-30, gamma 30-40 Hz
epoch_selection: ASR (channel r=0.75, burst 25 SD) + ICA/ICLabel (90% artefact prob.); first 100 s retained
time_since_dose: 1 h, 24 h, 7 d post-infusion analysed (EEG also recorded at 30 min during infusion but not analysed here)
quote: analyses were restricted to the first 100 s of data ... Continuous data were band-pass filtered (1-50 Hz, finite impulse response) and down-sampled to 250 Hz
notes: HOI computed per frequency band (not broadband for rest) on all n-plets of 15 electrodes. O-info is a multivariate information measure, borderline 'complexity'. MMN task analysis also (2 h, 7 d).

agent: ketamine (racemic, IV 0.5 mg/kg over 40 min) vs saline, crossover double-blind
measures: high-order interactions: TC, DTC, O-information, S-information (Gaussian-copula)
filter_type: NR (bandpass 0.5-40 Hz; band-specific delta 0.5-4, theta 4-8, alpha 8-12, beta 12-30, gamma 30-40 also analysed)
epoch_s: NR (valid time points pooled; epoch extraction mentioned without length)
data_per_condition_s: ~600 nominal (later half of 20-min rest during infusion) minus removed points
epoch_selection: proprietary Cumulus cloud QC pipeline; time points removed across all channels if any channel flat; later half of rest recording analysed
time_since_dose: during infusion: rest recorded in first 20 min of 40-min infusion, second half (approx. 10-20 min) analysed
quote: EEG signals were pre- processed with filtering from 0.5-40 Hz, epoch extraction, and baseline adjustment. All data were recorded with a left-mastoid reference.
notes: Broadband and per-band HOI. O-info is a multivariate information measure, borderline 'complexity'. MMN task during last 15 min of infusion also analysed (broadband).

agent: ketamine (racemic, IV 30-min infusion, 0.5-1 mg/kg; mean 0.7) during repeated-infusion course
measures: LZc (LZ76 per channel per epoch), CSER (state-space entropy rate, per band), plus PLE/IRASA aperiodic slope
data_per_condition_s: ~175-184 per state (3 min EO and 3 min EC each pre and post)
epoch_selection: ICA (runica) for muscle/blink/ocular/cardiac; noisy channels interpolated; all remaining 2-s epochs
time_since_dose: immediately after end of 30-min infusion (6 min post recording); pre-infusion baseline same session; recorded after patients had already responded (not first dose)
